contradictions.note: Backing would normally damage the rear. All damage in the estimate and photos is at the front-left, which fits the estimate's 'pulling into' account. The adjuster's note calls the photos consistent with an account they do not match. The intake loss description was not available to show which version the policyholder gave.
The estimate replaces the upper grille. The adjuster's damage list leaves it out, and the chrome grille in IMG_0071.jpg looks intact.

contradictions.topic: Bracket marked remove-and-reinstall but charged as a part
contradictions.note: R&I means the existing part is removed and reinstalled, yet the parts detail charges a new part with a part number. The shop should clarify. Separately, the fastener kit's part number uses a different platform code (SEA) from the other parts (TL2).

packet.rationale: The packet contains the claim and policy record from ClaimsPro and Snowflake, the shop estimate (repair_estimate.pdf, 4 pages), two damage photos (IMG_0071.jpg, IMG_0072.jpg) and the adjuster's notes (adjuster_notes.md). The evidence checklist is complete, and the estimate total of $2,825.07 adds up correctly and matches the claim amount, VIN and plate. The date of loss is not recorded anywhere, and the policy start and end dates are blank with policy status unknown. That means the adjuster's note that coverage was in force with 'no lapse at DOL' cannot be traced to anything on file. The deductible is also unconfirmed: the estimate shows 0.00 and the structured record has none. The sources disagree on how the loss happened: adjuster_notes.md calls it a 'backing incident', while repair_estimate.pdf says the vehicle struck a bollard while pulling into a space, which fits the front-left damage in the photos. The estimate also includes an upper grille that is not in the adjuster's damage list and looks intact in IMG_0071.jpg. Because the claim was closed as Paid in Full on 2025-06-20, it needs a person to obtain and record the date of loss, the coverage check and the policyholder's own account of the loss, and to look again at the file in light of those answers.
